title: Children's Civic Club — Session 3: Choices, Integrity & the Change Champion Box

slides.title: Welcome to the Civic Club!
slides.tip: Play welcome music. Make sure everyone is seated in their groups.

slides.title: Change Champion Zone
body: A box to capture your stories of change
slides.tip: Distribute Making Change Champion Box Instruction Annexure

slides.title: Hospital Stories
body: January 2019: Times of India, Chennai — Families of women who gave birth at a government hospital with free healthcare filed complaints today. They said they had to pay at least ₹3,500 in bribes to ward attendants, helpers, and other staff. The amount was even higher if a boy was born.

March 17, 2017: Hindustan Times, Hyderabad — Unable to pay a bribe for a wheelchair at the hospital, a patient used his son's toy tricycle. Since hospital attendants were demanding ₹100–200 for a wheelchair, the patient's wife started bringing her son's tricycle to take her husband inside during visits. 40-year-old Raju suffered burn injuries from an electric shock last August and has been visiting the hospital regularly for treatment. His wife Santoshi said that because she could not afford to give 'tips' to wardboys, they refused to provide a wheelchair — so they had to use the tricycle to get around the hospital.
slides.tip: Two news-based stories. Show images below.

slides.title: Discussion
body: Why do such things happen? How does this make you feel?
Who do you think is responsible for this?
Imagine for a moment how a person would feel when they are given a toy tricycle instead of a wheelchair.

slides.title: Group Work
body: Distribute sheets with stories or scenarios
One — list the value or quality shown by the story, something every good person should adopt
Two — an action or behaviour that demonstrates that specific value
slides.tip: Distribute Annexure 3 — one sheet per group.

slides.title: Example — Master Change explains

items.question: Which value am I not showing?
What positive action would show that value?

slides.transcript: MC gives a traffic-signal example: 'I always get late leaving home for school. To reach on time I sometimes break traffic signals. Which value am I not showing? — Not breaking signals, road awareness. Very good! Now what positive action would show that value? — Following rules, respect for other vehicles.'
kn_script: ನಾನು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಮನೆಯಿಂದ ಶಾಲೆಗೆ ಹೊರಡುವಾಗ ತಡವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಮಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ತಲುಪಲು, ನಾನು ಅನೇಕ ಬಾರಿ ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ ಸಿಗ್ನಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಮೀರುತ್ತೇನೆ.
ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಒಬ್ಬ ಉತ್ತಮ ಮನುಷ್ಯನಾಗಿ ನಾನು ಹೊಂದಿರಬೇಕಾದ ಆದರೆ ತೋರುತ್ತಿರದ 'ಮೌಲ್ಯ' ಯಾವುದು?
ತುಂಬಾ ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು! ಈಗ, ಈ ಕಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆ ಮೌಲ್ಯವನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುವ ಸಕಾರಾತ್ಮಕ ಕ್ರಮ ಯಾಮುದು?
en_script: I always get late leaving home for school. To reach on time, I sometimes break traffic signals.
As a good person, which value should I have but am not showing here?
Very good! Now, what positive action in this story would demonstrate that value?
slides.tip: Teacher clicks 'Next Question' after class discussion for each question. 2 questions total.

slides.title: Do the group work
body: Distribute the sheets to your groups.
7-minute timer starts. A warning buzzer will sound when 2 minutes remain.
slides.tip: Distribute Annexure 3 sheets. Each group gets a different sheet. 7-minute timer (use a watch if widget not available).

slides.title: Wrap up the group work
body: Thank you! You all did great work in your groups!
It's okay if you didn't finish — when we share with each other, all the stories and scenarios will be discussed.
Quickly pick two stories or scenarios that you would like to share with the whole class.
slides.tip: 1-minute timer. Each group should choose two stories.

slides.title: Share stories
body: One by one, one person from your group, please read one of your chosen stories to the class.
Do not repeat stories or scenarios.
slides.tip: Go to each group and ask them to share one story. Maintain discipline.

slides.title: Write on the board — Group summary
body: One member from each group, come to the board and write two action statements from your list.
You have only 1 minute, so be quick!
Come to any part of the board and write in big letters so everyone can read.
slides.tip: 1-minute timer. Make sure everyone has chalk.

slides.title: Let's reflect — 2 minutes of silence
body: Let us all silently reflect for a moment on what came out of your group discussions and what is written on the board.
You have 2 minutes to think and reflect.
slides.tip: As children start reflecting, encourage them to connect the values to the hospital story from the start of the session.

slides.title: ₹150 — What would you do?
slides.intro_text: A shopkeeper mistakenly gives you ₹150 extra change. What would you do?
post_video_text: What do we call this act of making a decision?
It starts with the letter C…
slides.tip: Give children time to answer. If they take too long, click REVEAL/NEXT to show CHOICE.

slides.title: Reflect on the hospital stories
kn_script: ಆರಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ ನಾನು ಓದಿದ ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆಯ ಕಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಬಡಜನರಿಗೆ ಯಾವ ಆಯ್ಕೆಗಳು ಇತ್ತು? ಅವರು ಒಂದುವೇಳೆ ಲಂಚವನ್ನು ಕೋಡದೇ ಇದ್ದರೆ, ಖಾಯಿಲೆಯಾಗಿರುವ ಅವರ ಪ್ರೀತಿಪಾತ್ರರಿಗೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?
ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆಯ ಕಥೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ, ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆಯ ಸಿಬ್ಬಂದಿ ಮಾಡಿದಂತಹ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಏನಾಗಿತ್ತು?
en_script: In the hospital stories I read at the beginning, what choices did the poor people have? If they didn't pay the bribe, what would happen to their sick loved ones?
In the hospital stories, what choice did the hospital staff make?
slides.transcript: Friends, in the hospital stories you read — what choice did poor people have? Sometimes poor people have very few choices. Poor people pay bribes out of compulsion.
slides.tip: MC draws children's attention back to the hospital stories. Allow time for discussion.

slides.title: What value do we build through the choices we make?
body: What value do we build through the choices we make?
slides.tip: After children answer, click REVEAL/NEXT. Show 'INTEGRITY' creatively.

slides.title: Everyday choices
kn_script: ಬನ್ನಿ, ಈಗ ನಾವು ನಮ್ಮ ಶಾಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾಡಬಹುದಾದ ಕೆಲವು ಆಯ್ಕೆಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡೋಣ
ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ಚಾಂಪಿಯನ್ ಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಗದೇ ಇರುವಂತಹ ಕಥೆಯನ್ನು ಬರೆದು ಹಾಕಿದರೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?
ನಾವು ಸುಳ್ಳನ್ನು ಬರೆದು ಹಾಕಿದರೆ ನಾವು ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ಚಾಂಪಿಯನ್ ಆಗುತ್ತೇವೆಯೇ?
ಖಾಲಿ ಚೀಟಿಗಳನ್ನು ಹಾಕುವುದು ಅಥವಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ಚಾಂಪಿಯನ್ ಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆಯನ್ನು ಹಾಳು ಮಾಡುವುದು - ಇವೆಲ್ಲವೂ ನಮ್ಮ ಬಗ್ಗೆ, ನಮ್ಮ ತರಗತಿ, ನಮ್ಮ ಕ್ಲಬ್ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಏನನ್ನು ಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ?
ನಾವು ನಮ್ಮ ಯೋಜನಾ ಕಾರ್ಯವನ್ನು ಗೂಗಲ್ ನಿಂದ ಅಥವಾ ಚಾಟ್ ಜಿಪಿಟಿ ಬಳಸಿ ನಕಲು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ, ಸ್ವತಃ ನಾವೇ ಮಾಡದೇ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?
ನಾವು ನಿಜವಾಗಿಯೂ ಮಾಡದೇ ಇರುವ ಸಂಗತಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಪಡಿಸಬೇಕಾದಾಗ ನಮಗೆ ಹೇಗೆನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?
en_script: Come, let us now talk about some choices we can make at our school.
What happens if we write a story in the Change Champion Box about something that didn't actually happen?
If we write lies, do we become Change Champions?
Putting in blank slips or spoiling the Change Champion Box — what does all this say about us, our class, our club?
What happens if we copy our project work from Google or ChatGPT instead of doing it ourselves?
How do we feel when we have to present something we didn't actually do?
slides.transcript: MC talks about daily choices at school — spoiled Change Champion Box, copying from ChatGPT, helping absent friends, admitting a broken window. Ends with 'your daily choices make you a real change champion'.
slides.tip: Give children time to respond after each scenario.

slides.title: Think about it
body: Through every small choice, what kind of person are we becoming?

slides.title: Two sides of a coin
body: Every coin has two sides. In life too, every issue has more than one perspective.
Draw a picture of both sides of a coin.
Side A: Something they value — something every good person should adopt (e.g. honesty, friendship, fun)
Side B: A challenge or the opposite idea (e.g. dishonesty, conflict, boredom)
slides.tip: Show only if time permits. Optional.

slides.title: Two sides of a coin — Reflect
body: What happens if we only look at one side of the coin?
How does looking at both sides within ourselves help us make fair choices?

slides.title: Start — Stop — Continue
body: Based on what you learned today:
What is one new thing you want to START doing in your life?
What is one thing you want to STOP doing?
What is something you are already doing that you want to CONTINUE?
slides.tip: Give each child time to share one answer.

slides.title: Thank you!
